sources.title: Each company's public pricing pages and terms, linked from its BackPR comparison page

resources.notes: BackPR competes with the companies in this index, so we left BackPR out. A value of "not published" means we found nothing, not that the company doesn't offer it. CC BY 4.0 covers BackPR's compilation; quoted company text remains the company's. Companies in the index can send corrections to support@backpr.com. resources.name: youth-nonprofits-by-state-json
resources.title: Youth and community nonprofits by state: active 501(c)(3) organizations from IRS data
resources.description: Counts of active 501(c)(3) youth development, amateur sports, PTA and PTO, recreation, camp and club, children's and youth services, arts education and childcare nonprofits in each state and DC, by group, including how many report under $50,000 in annual revenue. There are 171,592 nationally. The state rows total 171,286; the other 306 have no state on file or are in US territories, at military addresses or abroad.
resources.cite_as: BackPR (2026). Youth and community nonprofits by state: active 501(c)(3) organizations from IRS data (version 1.0, checked September 2026). https://backpr.com/data/youth-nonprofits-by-state.json. CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File, posted September 8, 2026

resources.notes: Filter: Active 501(c)(3) organizations in the NTEE codes listed for each group. Group codes (NTEE, the IRS's activity codes for nonprofits): Amateur sports: N40, N6x, N7x; Youth development: all O codes; PTAs and PTOs: B94; Recreation, camps and clubs: N20, N30, N31, N50; Children's and youth services: P30; Arts education: A25; Childcare: P33. Each organization is counted once, by its main NTEE code. Some groups, such as amateur sports and arts education, include organizations that also serve adults. The "under_50k" column counts organizations that report annual revenue under $50,000 on their latest IRS filing or have no revenue amount on file.

resources.name: child-care-capacity-by-state-json
resources.title: Licensed child care capacity by state: seats per 100 children
resources.description: Licensed seats and programs in each state's public child care licensing data, compared with the number of children aged 0 to 12, plus staff-to-child ratios.
resources.cite_as: BackPR (2026). Licensed child care capacity by state: seats per 100 children (snapshot 2026-11-08). https://backpr.com/data/child-care-capacity-by-state.json. CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: Each state's official child care licensing data, as listed per record
U.S. Census Bureau, Vintage 2024 population estimates by age (civilian), July 1, 2024

resources.notes: Seats are the licensed capacity each state publishes for licensed child care centers and school-age programs in its open data. Home-based family child care isn't included. Capacity is the most children a program may care for at once, not enrollment or open spots. Children are ages 0 to 12, from July 1, 2024 estimates; seats are from the snapshot date. States where fewer than 95% of listings publish a capacity have a minimum seat count and are left out of per-child figures, totals and scores. States without a statewide list with capacity have no per-child figure. Scores (0 to 100) rank a state against the other states with a per-child figure; for ratios, fewer children per adult scores higher.

resources.name: child-care-cost-by-state-json
resources.title: Child care cost by state and county: median weekly prices and share of family income
resources.description: County median weekly child care prices for infants, toddlers, preschool and school-age children in centers and family child care homes, with cost as a share of median family income, from the U.S. Department of Labor Women's Bureau National Database of Childcare Prices.
resources.cite_as: BackPR (2026). Child care cost by state and county, from the U.S. Department of Labor Women's Bureau National Database of Childcare Prices (2022 data). https://backpr.com/data/child-care-cost-by-state.json. CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: U.S. Department of Labor, Women's Bureau, National Database of Childcare Prices (county file 2008-2022; technical report September 2024)

resources.notes: Weekly full-time median prices from state market rate surveys, standardized by the Women's Bureau contractor; prices are in the dollars of the study year and are not inflation-adjusted. Many 2022 values are estimates between survey years or filled in from state data; see the technical report. Cost as a share of income is BackPR's calculation: weekly price x 52 divided by the county's median family income (ACS, same year). A state's typical county is the median of its county medians, not weighted by population.
